$comment: Externalized harness policy data (HARNESS-020). The scan ENGINE lives in scripts/harness/*; this file holds the project-specific POLICY so the engine is repo-agnostic. Edit values here instead of hardcoding literals in scan scripts.

architectureDocs.$comment: Canonical architecture documents whose prose/diagrams must reference only real workspace packages (check-dependency-direction Rule 9, absorbed from check-architecture-conformance.mjs). packages/*/docs/SPEC.md is always included by the engine.

purity.$comment: Package-purity POLICY (check-dependency-direction Rule 10, absorbed from check-sdk-react-free.mjs). Each entry forbids a package from importing OR declaring the listed modules; a missing scan target is a hard finding, not a silent pass (HARNESS-016 / ARL-16g dead-guard guard).
purity.reason: agent-framework is a platform-neutral assembly layer; React hooks/context/components belong in the product/UI packages (agent-cli, agent-transport-tui, agent-transport-gui) only.

consistency.$comment: Policy DATA for scan-consistency.mjs (HARNESS-DIET-003 split). The engine (five exported check functions) lives in scripts/harness/scan-consistency.mjs; the Robota-specific required-script names, guidance scan targets, and phrase blocklists live here. `pattern` fields are RegExp sources (compiled with the optional `flags`). Values moved VERBATIM from the former in-script constants.

compositionNeutrality.$comment: ARCH-005 composition-neutrality POLICY (scan-composition-neutrality.mjs). Enforces the three R1 guards that make the agent-product L129 carve-out safe: the shared assembler stays pure, IO-free, and product-neutral. The amended project-structure L129 rule is COUPLED to these guards. A missing scan target is a hard finding, not a silent pass.
compositionNeutrality.reason: agent-product is the pure, IO-free, product-neutral assembler (assembleProduct). Its L129 carve-out holds ONLY while it takes no concrete transport/TUI/CLI dep (a), reads no fs/env/settings (b — resolved data is fed in from the shell), and branches on no product identity (c).

HARNESS-048: agent-capability-pack is the other half of the ARCH-005 composition contract — the additive capability-bundle type plus the pure mergeCapabilityPacks fold that assembleProduct applies. It is an equally pure PUBLISHED contract package, so the same three guards apply: it must take no concrete transport/TUI/CLI dep (a), read no fs/env/settings (b), and branch on no product identity (c) — a merger that special-cases one product's pack ids is a shared product factory wearing a merge function's clothes.

neutrality.$comment: Per-subsystem library-neutrality policy DATA (HARNESS-DIET-002). The neutrality scan ENGINES live in scripts/harness/scan-*-neutrality.mjs; their Robota-specific target paths / allowlists / forbidden terms live here so the engines stay repo-agnostic.

progressReportQuantification.$comment: Policy DATA for scan-progress-report-quantification.mjs (HARNESS-026). The ENGINE (transcript streaming, narrative extraction, bare-ratio detection, suppression) lives in scripts/harness/scan-progress-report-quantification.mjs; the host-specific transcript root, the enforcement cutoff, and the keyword vocabulary live here. `*Pattern` fields are RegExp sources matched case-insensitively. transcriptRoot is the agent harness's per-project session-transcript directory (a leading `~` expands to the home directory); when it has no directory for this workspace the scan SKIPS with an explicit reason. enforceSinceIso is a TIME RATCHET: conversation before it cannot be edited, so only sessions from adoption onward are judged — move it forward only to adopt a deliberate, reviewed reset. completionKeywordPattern gates a line to completion/progress context; identifierNounPattern suppresses reference forms (Step 2/3, lines 54/146) that are not counts.

promptProse.$comment: Policy DATA for scan-prompt-prose.mjs (NEUT-006, audit 2026-07-24 gap #6). The ENGINE (literal extraction, prose heuristic, frozen-baseline ratchet, role-vocab conjunction) lives in scripts/harness/scan-prompt-prose.mjs; the Robota-specific scan roots, prompt-sink patterns, exemptions, and role vocabulary live here. `pattern` fields are RegExp sources. exemptPathIncludes lists the CHARTERED opinion homes (audit: personas/presets are quarantined opinion, not neutral-library debt); roleVocabulary flags a workflow role name AND a concrete model id in the SAME file (the role→model opinion) outside allowedPathIncludes.

authorityBypass.reason: The task-run transition table is the single place the legal transitions live, so a status written as a literal is one the table never authorised.
Same rule for the run's own state machine.
This helper lands a task in a terminal status; a literal here launders the same bypass through one more call.

rolePortOptionals.$comment: ARCH-029 TC-06: role ports carry zero optional members. An aggregate-level ceiling would NOT have caught the regression this guards — `getAgentJobCapability?()` adds 15 reachable members while contributing 1 to any optional count, and `getSession()` adds 18 while contributing 0. A member may be optional only when its VALUE is genuinely variational, never because a host might not implement it; each such member is carved out below with a reason.

carveOuts.reason: A genuinely variational adapter bag: its CONTENTS differ by host by design, so requiring it would force every host to answer a question with no single answer. This is the distinction the rule keeps — variational value, not unimplemented member.

aggregateNaming.$comment: ARCH-029: the load-bearing floor. A god contract is not fixed by decomposing it — it is fixed when consumers stop NAMING it, and REFACTOR-006 proved those are different events (it closed green on the same contract, which then grew 20 members/50% optional to 46/70%). Type-position references to each aggregate are frozen in scripts/harness/aggregate-naming-baseline.json; they may fall and must never rise. The target is 0, not 'falling'.
aggregateNaming.$scopeNote: ICommandHostContext is the criterion ARCH-029 drives to ZERO (TC-05). The other two aggregates were decomposed by the same change but their consumer migration is NOT in this item's approved scope — they are frozen at what they measure today so the decomposition cannot regrow, and reaching zero is tracked separately. Freezing them at a non-zero number is the split the design sanctions ('TC-05a freezes, TC-05b reaches 0'), not a weakening of TC-05.

allowlist.reason: Declares ICommandHostContext as an empty `extends` over its role ports.
Declares ICommandSessionRuntime as an empty `extends` over its role ports.
Declares IAgentJobHostContext as an empty `extends` over its role ports.
The conformant IAgentJobHostContext double — it exists to be checked against the whole aggregate with no cast.
The declaration site. The aggregate is defined here as an empty `extends` over the role ports.

`ISystemCommand.execute`'s parameter — the dispatch contract every command is assigned to. A command narrows its own declared role against this by contravariance; this one site must name the widest type.

The dispatch spine. It holds the host and hands it to an arbitrary `ISystemCommand.execute`, so it cannot know which roles the callee needs and must name the widest type — the same reason the contract itself is allowlisted.
Supplies the host to that same dispatch spine (`getSession: () => ICommandHostContext`). Narrowing here would narrow what every routed command can reach.
The production host. `implements ICommandHostContext` is the compiler-checked conformance ARCH-029 TC-01 installed; naming it here is the check, not a leak.
The conformant double. It exists to be checked against the whole aggregate with no cast — that is its entire property.

renameCarveOuts.reason: The role-port method that reaches the session aggregate — the decomposition's own wiring. ICommandHostContext composes ICommandHostSessionAccess, and a command narrows to this port precisely so it can reach the session runtime; a host that could not return it would not be a host. Named here rather than exempted structurally: a blanket MethodSignature skip is an unnamed, non-expiring exemption over an unbounded set, and it covered every future method-signature handle in all ten allowlisted files in order to spare this site and one other.

The second and last site that forces a method-signature exemption. Same reason as the sibling entry: the agent-job aggregate is reached through this port by design. The `| undefined` is part of the asserted type, so narrowing or widening it expires this carve-out and rename-carve-out-unused reports it.

The options bag of the conformant ICommandHostContext double. A double that exists to be checked against the whole aggregate with no cast must let a caller state overrides against that same aggregate, so this member cannot be written any other way. It IS an addressable handle and this carve-out does not claim otherwise: review compiled the proof that keyof over TOverrides<ICommandHostContext> yields the full member-name list and that each member type is recoverable and callable by indexed access, with the aggregate never named. That is a STATED LIMIT of a name-only walk, recorded in scan-aggregate-naming.mjs alongside the ReturnType<typeof createTestCommandHost> route; closing either needs the type checker. An earlier revision of this reason claimed a mapped type hands out no second handle, and that was false.
Same site, same reason and the same stated limit, for the session-runtime half of the double options bag.

contractCastRatchet.$comment: ARCH-012: contracts whose `as X` cast count is frozen by scan-contract-cast-ratchet. A cast is a partial re-implementation nothing checks against the real contract; the count may fall and never rise while capability-scoped ports are designed.

optionReachability.name: ICreateSessionOptions
optionReachability.reason: The session-construction option surface. `guardrails` (SELFHOST-005) and `retrievalAdapter` (SELFHOST-003) were declared, read at the consuming end, and set by no production call to createSession — two documented capabilities no shipped surface could turn on.

productIdentity.$comment: NEUT-009: a library must not name its consumer's product. Per-package occurrence counts are frozen in scripts/harness/product-identity-baseline.json — they may fall and must never rise. Markers must NOT overlap: `~/.robota` was removed because `.robota` already matches it and every such line was counted twice.
